I would calculate the RMD using the age-83 Uniform Lifetime divisor of 17.7: $1,590,000 ÷ 17.7 = about $89,831. The $53,500 QCD is excluded from taxable income, leaving about $36,331 of taxable IRA income. Social Security is taxable up to 85% because provisional income exceeds the upper threshold: $30,600. AGI is therefore about $90,931 including the $24,000 pension. After the standard deduction and age-65 addition, plus the $6,000 senior deduction, taxable income is about $54,000. Applying the single brackets gives roughly $6,200 tax.
ANSWER: 6200

A qualified charitable distribution is not included in income, so the IRA amount counted is $26,000. Provisional income is $26,000 + $12,500 tax-exempt interest + half of $45,000 Social Security ($22,500), or $61,000. That exceeds the joint upper threshold, so 85% of benefits are taxable: $38,250. The taxable benefit calculation also remains under the 85% cap.
ANSWER: 38250

Their provisional income includes pension, IRA distributions, tax-exempt interest, and half of Social Security. Social Security totals $46,800, so baseline MAGI is $54,000 + $78,500 + $39,780 = $172,280; IRMAA MAGI adds $7,500 municipal interest, for $179,780. The next joint IRMAA tier begins at $218,000 (2026 tier assumption). A Roth conversion increases MAGI dollar for dollar, so the headroom is $38,220.
ANSWER: 38220

Baseline IRMAA MAGI includes taxable income plus tax-exempt interest. At these income levels 85% of Social Security is taxable: $27,540. MAGI is $39,500 + $26,200 + $27,540 = $93,240, and with $23,500 municipal interest it is $116,740. The next single IRMAA tier begins at $109,000, so they are already above it; any conversion raises the premium tier relative to no conversion only if it crosses the next breakpoint, $136,000. Headroom is $19,260.
ANSWER: 19260

The QCD portion is excluded; taxable IRA income is $11,597. Provisional income is $11,597 + $8,500 tax-exempt interest + $16,500 half benefits = $36,597. This puts benefits at the 85% cap for a single filer: $28,050. (The taxable-benefit formula reaches the cap at this provisional income.)
ANSWER: 28050

Without conversion, half of their $54,000 Social Security is $27,000, so provisional income is $80,500 and 85% of benefits ($45,900) is taxable. With the $80,000 conversion, provisional income rises and the same 85% taxable cap applies. The federal taxable income rises by $80,000 and is taxed at the applicable marginal rates; Arizona starts from federal income, subtracts the federal senior deduction, and uses its 2.5% rate. Combining the federal incremental tax and the Arizona increase gives approximately $17,600.
ANSWER: 17600

For an eligible designated beneficiary who is not within an exception, the 10-year rule applies, but because the original owner had begun RMDs, annual beneficiary RMDs continue during the 10-year period. For an adult child, the life expectancy factor is based on the beneficiary’s age in the year after death, reduced by one each year. Gideon was 60 in 2024, giving an initial factor of 27.1; by 2026 it is 25.1. $474,000 ÷ 25.1 is about $18,884.
ANSWER: 18884

At age 82, Greta’s RMD divisor is 18.5, so the distribution is $1,390,000 ÷ 18.5 = about $75,135. Subtracting the $18,500 QCD leaves $56,635 taxable IRA income. 85% of $31,200 Social Security is $26,520, and pension income is $500, so AGI is about $83,655. After the standard deduction, age deduction, and $6,000 senior deduction, taxable income is roughly $40,000, producing about $4,400 federal tax.
ANSWER: 4400

Social Security taxation is determined using pension, interest, and half of benefits: $38,000 + $2,000 + $10,200 = $50,200 provisional income. Thus 85% of benefits, $17,340, is taxable; federal income is $57,340. Arizona begins from federal income, subtracts the federal senior deduction, and applies its standard deduction equal to the federal basic amount. The resulting Arizona taxable base is about $34,000. At Arizona’s 2.5% rate the tax is approximately $850.
ANSWER: 850

At age 80, the Uniform Lifetime divisor is 20.2, so the RMD is $830,000 ÷ 20.2 = about $41,089. Subtracting the $10,000 QCD leaves $31,089 taxable IRA income. 85% of Social Security is $22,950; with the $7,000 pension, AGI is approximately $61,039. After the standard deduction, age addition, and $6,000 senior deduction, taxable income is around $36,000. Applying the single tax brackets gives about $3,900.
ANSWER: 3900

Half of Social Security is $13,200. Provisional income is $37,500 + $69,300 + $15,000 + $13,200 = $135,000, so 85% of benefits ($22,440) is taxable. IRMAA MAGI is $129,240 plus the $15,000 tax-exempt interest, or $144,240. The next single tier starts at $171,000, making conversion headroom $26,760.
ANSWER: 26760
